## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized polypore mushroom characterized by a tan to brown cap, a central to slightly off-center stalk, and large angular pores on the underside instead of gills. In Florida, the Spring Polypore grows on dead hardwood branches, fallen logs, stumps, and buried woody debris in hammocks, hardwood forests, mixed woods, parks, and shaded yards. It acts as a wood-decay fungus, breaking down dead plant material and helping recycle nutrients back into the forest floor.
